docs.text: Setup Guide You can refer to the official documentation below for instructions on how to set up an Astar Archive Node . 🔗 Archive Node A node can be set up on a physical machine, virtual machine, container environment, or cloud instance. However, any setup other than a physical machine requires a significant amount of infrastructure-related technical knowledge. For those who are not technical specialists, we recommend starting by preparing a physical machine . Docker The configuration using Docker is documented in the official guide. 🔗 Dokcker Docker Compose For reference, here is an example procedure for setting up an archive node using Docker Compose. 🔗 How to create an Archive Node with Docker compose.yml / Author: Dagga Astar Releases The release provides binaries for macOS x86_64, Ubuntu x86_64, and Linux ARM64 (aarch64). 🔗 Latest Release Additional Information Before setting up, I’ll provide some supplementary notes to the official documentation. About Machine Specifications As of December 2025 , the HDD currently in use occupies 1.73 TB . Since blockchain data storage functions as a type of database, performance is just as important as capacity, and for physical machines, power consumption becomes an additional critical factor. Although SSDs are recommended, HDDs can also be used. However, HDDs require careful attention to power supply, and USB bus‑powered connections are not recommended. It is safer to have at least 8 GB of RAM . There are cases where Raspberry Pi 4/5 with 4 GB RAM have operated successfully, but machines with 8 GB or more tend to be more stable.

docs.text: Maintenance tips Replace the HDD XFS Archive Node: Migrating Data from a 2TB HDD to a 5TB HDD (USB / Ubuntu 24.04 LTS) Introduction This document describes the procedure used to migrate data from a 2TB HDD to a larger 5TB HDD on an archive node. The migration was required due to increasing disk usage on the running node. The environment uses: Ubuntu 24.04 LTS XFS filesystem USB‑connected portable HDDs (2TB and 5TB) This guide is intended to help other operators performing similar maintenance. System Overview Role Machine Description Production archive node Machine A 2TB HDD mounted at /var/lib/astar Migration workstation Machine B Used to connect both 2TB and 5TB HDDs Data Migration Procedure 1. Work on Machine A (Detach the device) Stop the running service # sudo systemctl stop astar.service Unmount the data directory # sudo umount /var/lib/astar 2. Work on Machine B (Migration) 2-1. Connect disks and verify devices Connect both the 2TB and 5TB HDDs (physical work) Check device information # lsblk -o NAME,SIZE,TYPE,MODEL Example: sdc 1.8T disk ST2000LM007-1R8174 └─sdc1 1.8T part sdd 4.5T disk WDC WD50NDZW-11BCSS0 └─sdd1 4.5T part sdc → 2TB HDD sdd → 5TB HDD 2-2. Create a partition on the 5TB HDD Create a GPT label # sudo parted /dev/sdd mklabel gpt ⚠ Note on alignment warnings Running: # sudo parted -a optimal /dev/sdd mkpart primary xfs 0% 100% may produce: The closest location we can manage is 17.4kB to 1048kB (sectors 34..2047). This indicates the partition does not start on a 2048‑sector (1MiB) boundary. Proper alignment is important for performance and should not be ignored. ✔ Correct partition creation (aligned at 1MiB) # sudo parted -a optimal /dev/sdd mkpart primary xfs 1MiB 100% 2-3. Verify the partition # lsblk -o NAME,SIZE,FSTYPE,MOUNTPOINT /dev/sdd Example: sdd 4.5T └─sdd1 4.5T ntfs 2-4. Create an XFS filesystem # sudo mkfs.xfs -f /dev/sdd1 (Output omitted) 2-5. Confirm XFS creation # lsblk -o NAME,SIZE,FSTYPE,MOUNTPOINT /dev/sdd sdd 4.5T └─sdd1 4.5T xfs 2-6. Mount both disks # sudo mkdir /a /b # sudo mount /dev/sdc1 /a # sudo mount /dev/sdd1 /b Verify: # lsblk -o NAME,SIZE,FSTYPE,MOUNTPOINT /dev/sdc /dev/sdd 2-7. Perform XFS dump & restore (core migration step) Dump from 2TB → Restore to 5TB # sudo xfsdump -J - /a | sudo xfsrestore -J - /b This process took approximately 15 hours over USB 3.0. (Output omitted) 2-8. Verify migrated data # sudo ls -al /b 2-9. Optional: XFS integrity check Unmount the restored filesystem # sudo umount /b Run a read‑only check # sudo xfs_repair -n /dev/sdd1 (Output omitted) 2-10. Unmount and remove disks # sudo sync # sudo umount /a # sudo umount /b Then physically disconnect both HDDs. 3. Work on Machine A (Reconnect and resume service) Connect the 5TB HDD (physical work) Verify the device # lsblk -o NAME,SIZE,FSTYPE,MOUNTPOINT /dev/sdb Example: sdb 4.5T └─sdb1 4.5T xfs Mount the new disk # sudo mount /dev/sdb1 /var/lib/astar Start the service # sudo systemctl start astar.service Monitor logs # journalctl -f -u astar.service -n 100

docs.text: Join the Astar Peers Program The Astar Peers Program welcomes community members who want to support the decentralization of Astar Network while gaining practical experience in Linux and blockchain infrastructure. Participation is open to applicants from any region. Some places are prioritized to improve the geographic diversity of the network. Season 3.1 Recruitment Applications for Season 3.1 are now open. Application Deadline: August 31, 2026, at 23:59 UTC Applications submitted after the deadline may not be considered. Who Can Apply? You may apply if you: Have basic experience using Linux Can prepare and maintain a supported machine Can run an Astar archive node Can connect the node to Polkadot Telemetry Can operate the node with no major interruptions and aim for at least 80% uptime Are willing to participate for the relevant program season For detailed hardware and software conditions, see Machine and Technical Requirements . Regional Selection For Season 3.1, the program plans to select 5 node operators: At least five candidates from the program's priority regions The priority regions are South America, Africa, West Asia, Southeast Asia, and Australia. At present, participants are selected by tksarah , the program administrator. Before You Apply Please confirm that: [ ] I have basic Linux experience. [ ] I can prepare an ARM or x86_64 machine that meets the program requirements. [ ] My machine has at least 4 GB of RAM; 8 GB or more is recommended. [ ] My machine has at least 3 TB of HDD or SSD. [ ] I understand that I must operate an archive node. [ ] I can connect my node to Polkadot Telemetry. [ ] I can aim for at least 80% uptime. [ ] I have reviewed the Node Operation Rules . [ ] I understand the Rewards and Payments policy. Application and Selection Process Review the program information Read the program overview, technical requirements, operating rules, and reward policy. Confirm your environment Make sure you can prepare a suitable machine, storage, internet connection, and Linux environment. Submit your application Use the official application form or instructions announced for the relevant season. Program review The program administrator reviews applicants based on eligibility, regional priorities, and the number of available places. Selection and onboarding Selected participants receive the information needed to prepare, register, and begin operating their nodes. Begin node operation Participants run an archive node, connect it to Polkadot Telemetry, and maintain it throughout the season. Related Pages Program Overview Machine and Technical Requirements Node Operation Rules Rewards and Payments

docs.text: Node Operation Rules This page explains the responsibilities of participants after they have been selected for the Astar Peers Program. 1. Operate an Archive Node The node registered with the program must be an Astar archive node . Participants are responsible for maintaining the machine, operating system, node software, storage, and internet connection needed to keep the node synchronized and active. 2. Connect to Polkadot Telemetry Every participating node must be connected to Polkadot Telemetry . Telemetry allows the program to confirm that the node is visible, synchronized, and actively participating in the network. Participants should regularly check that: Their node appears under the expected node name The node remains synchronized The node has not disappeared because of a service, machine, or connection failure 3. Aim for at Least 80% Uptime Continuous 100% uptime is not required. However, participants are expected to operate their nodes without major interruptions and maintain at least 80% uptime as the program target. Reward eligibility is reviewed using the previous month's operating status. The current reward wording grants the full availability-based reward when uptime is 80% or more and a reduced reward when it is below 80% . See Rewards and Payments for the payment categories. 4. Monitor the Node Participants should regularly confirm: The machine is running The node process or service is active The node is synchronized Sufficient storage remains available Memory usage is within a stable range The node remains visible in Polkadot Telemetry The program does not require enterprise-level monitoring, but participants must be able to identify and respond to a stopped or unhealthy node. 5. Handle Interruptions and Resynchronization If a node stops because of a machine failure, software problem, storage issue, or network interruption, the participant should begin recovery as soon as reasonably possible. A node that is actively being restored or resynchronized may receive 30% of the standard reward for the relevant assessment period. Participants should keep the program administrator informed when: A node will be offline for an extended period Hardware must be repaired or replaced A full resynchronization is required The node cannot return to service 6. Avoid Long-Term Inactivity No reward is provided when a node is not operating or is considered inactive. Nodes may also become ineligible for rewards if they: Remain inactive for a long period Go offline frequently Repeatedly fail to maintain synchronization 7. Register an On-Chain Identity Participants should register the required on-chain identity for the account used in the program. If an on-chain identity is not registered, the reward is reduced by 50%. The program administrator should provide the identity format and verification procedure used for each season. 8. Participate in Program Reviews Regular reviews are conducted to evaluate the current season’s achievements, the remaining reward budget, and any continuation proposals in preparation for the next season. Monthly Operating Checklist [ ] My archive node is running. [ ] My node is synchronized. [ ] My node is visible in Polkadot Telemetry. [ ] My machine has sufficient free storage. [ ] My node has not experienced an unexplained long-term outage. [ ] I have reported any major interruption or resynchronization. [ ] My required on-chain identity is registered. Related Pages Program Overview How to Join Machine and Technical Requirements Rewards and Payments

docs.text: Astar Peers Program Empowering Astar Through Decentralization Decentralization is one of the core values of Astar Network. It is more than an ideal. It is the foundation of a resilient, efficient, and sustainable network. When nodes are distributed across more regions and operated by a wider range of participants, Astar becomes stronger, fairer, and more dependable. The Astar Peers Program turns this principle into practical action. By bringing together community members around the world, the program helps Astar grow into a truly global and sustainable network. Our Objectives 1. Strengthen the Decentralization of Astar Network The program expands community-operated nodes across different parts of the world. By encouraging participation from diverse regions, it aims to improve the resilience and long-term sustainability of Astar Network. 2. Develop Future Technical Contributors The program also helps participants build practical technical skills. An individual node may appear to be a small contribution. Together, however, these nodes form an important part of the Astar ecosystem. Through hands-on operation, participants learn how their own work contributes to a larger decentralized network. Blockchain nodes are often expected to run on high-performance, highly available infrastructure. The Astar Peers Program instead encourages participants to operate archive nodes on relatively modest machines. This makes node operation more accessible while providing valuable experience with Linux and blockchain infrastructure. How the Program Works Community members apply for a program season. Selected participants prepare a supported machine and run an Astar archive node. Each node is connected to Polkadot Telemetry and operated on an ongoing basis. Node activity is reviewed, and eligible participants receive a monthly reward in ASTR. Priority Regions Participation is open worldwide. The program gives particular attention to regions where greater infrastructure diversity can strengthen the network: South America Africa West Asia Southeast Asia — partially achieved during Seasons 1 and 2 Australia — partially achieved during Seasons 1 and 2 Season 3.1 at a Glance Date Milestone July 2026 Season 3.1 recruitment opens August 31, 2026 Application deadline March 2027 Mid-season review September 2027 Final review and preparation for Season 4 Learn More How to Join Machine and Technical Requirements Node Operation Rules Rewards and Payments Original program page: Astar Peers Program

docs.text: Machine and Technical Requirements Before applying to the Astar Peers Program, confirm that you can prepare an environment capable of running an Astar archive node on an ongoing basis. Supported Machine Types The program supports the following machine architectures: Category Supported examples ARM Raspberry Pi 4, Raspberry Pi 5, and other small ARM-based machines x86_64 Desktop computers, mini PCs, servers, and other compatible x86_64 machines The program encourages the use of relatively modest hardware. Enterprise-class infrastructure is not required. Memory Minimum: 4 GB RAM Recommended: 8 GB RAM or more Experience from Seasons 1 and 2 showed that machines with only 4 GB of physical memory—especially ARM-based machines—may have difficulty remaining stable over long periods. They are more likely to hang or shut down unexpectedly. For this reason, 8 GB or more is strongly recommended for stable operation. Storage The node must run as an archive node , which retains the complete blockchain state and history required by the node configuration. Currently, 3 TB or more of storage is required. Confirm the current storage needs of an Astar archive node before applying Prepare enough free capacity for continued chain growth Use storage suitable for continuous read and write activity Allow sufficient time and capacity for initial synchronization or resynchronization Internet Connection The current program rules do not define a minimum bandwidth or data allowance. However, the node must: Maintain a stable connection for ongoing synchronization Remain reachable enough to meet the program's uptime expectation Connect to Polkadot Telemetry Support the data transfer required for initial synchronization and future resynchronization Participants should avoid connections with restrictive data caps or frequent interruptions. Operating System and Linux Skills No specific Linux distribution is mandated in the current program rules. The selected operating environment must be able to run the supported Astar node software. Applicants must have at least basic Linux experience. You should be able to: Connect to and operate a Linux machine Run commands in a terminal Install and update required software Check processes, services, storage, and memory Read basic system and application logs Restart a stopped service or machine Follow node installation and troubleshooting instructions Building an archive node is relatively straightforward, but maintaining one requires basic Linux system administration skills. Node Configuration Requirements Every program node must: Run as an Astar archive node Connect to Polkadot Telemetry Operate without major interruptions Aim for at least 80% uptime For ongoing responsibilities, see Node Operation Rules . Related Pages Program Overview How to Join Node Operation Rules Rewards and Payments

docs.title: Supported Machine Types

docs.text: Minimum: 4 GB RAM Recommended: 8 GB RAM or more Experience from Seasons 1 and 2 showed that machines with only 4 GB of physical memory—especially ARM-based machines—may have difficulty remaining stable over long periods. They are more likely to hang or shut down unexpectedly. For this reason, 8 GB or more is strongly recommended for stable operation.
docs.title: Memory

docs.text: The node must run as an archive node , which retains the complete blockchain state and history required by the node configuration. Currently, 3 TB or more of storage is required. Confirm the current storage needs of an Astar archive node before applying Prepare enough free capacity for continued chain growth Use storage suitable for continuous read and write activity Allow sufficient time and capacity for initial synchronization or resynchronization
docs.title: Storage

docs.text: The current program rules do not define a minimum bandwidth or data allowance. However, the node must: Maintain a stable connection for ongoing synchronization Remain reachable enough to meet the program's uptime expectation Connect to Polkadot Telemetry Support the data transfer required for initial synchronization and future resynchronization Participants should avoid connections with restrictive data caps or frequent interruptions.
docs.title: Internet Connection

docs.text: No specific Linux distribution is mandated in the current program rules. The selected operating environment must be able to run the supported Astar node software. Applicants must have at least basic Linux experience. You should be able to: Connect to and operate a Linux machine Run commands in a terminal Install and update required software Check processes, services, storage, and memory Read basic system and application logs Restart a stopped service or machine Follow node installation and troubleshooting instructions Building an archive node is relatively straightforward, but maintaining one requires basic Linux system administration skills.
docs.title: Operating System and Linux Skills

docs.text: Every program node must: Run as an Astar archive node Connect to Polkadot Telemetry Operate without major interruptions Aim for at least 80% uptime For ongoing responsibilities, see Node Operation Rules .
docs.title: Node Configuration Requirements

docs.text: Rewards and Payments The Astar Peers Program provides a monthly reward to help participants cover part of the cost of operating a node. The reward is not intended to reimburse all expenses. It is a contribution toward recurring costs such as hardware, electricity, storage, and internet access. Base Reward The base reward is: USD 30 equivalent per month, paid in ASTR The actual number of ASTR tokens is adjusted using the relevant ASTR price and the 30-day Exponential Moving Average (EMA30). View the ASTR price reference chart Reward Categories Node or participant status Reward rate Uptime 80% or more 100% Uptime below 80% 50% Node is being restored or resynchronized 30% Node is not operating or is inactive 0% Required on-chain identity is not registered 50% reduction Nodes that remain inactive for a long period, go offline frequently, or fail to stay synchronized are not eligible for rewards. Example Amounts The examples below show the USD-equivalent value before conversion to ASTR: Reward rate USD-equivalent amount 100% USD 30 50% USD 15 30% USD 9 0% USD 0 The final payment is made in ASTR, so the token amount varies with the price used for conversion. On-Chain Identity Adjustment If the required on-chain identity is not registered, no reward will be provided even if the node meets the uptime requirements. Please note this. ASTR Conversion The base reward is denominated as USD 30. Payment is made in ASTR. The final ASTR amount is adjusted using EMA30. The value on the first day of the operating month is applied as the conversion rate. Payment Schedule As a general rule: The previous month's node activity is reviewed. The applicable reward rate is determined. The USD-equivalent reward is converted to ASTR. Payment is made during the current month. Reward Funding Rewards are paid from the program wallet balance secured during the previous season. If additional funding becomes necessary for future operation of the program, a new proposal may be considered.
